accuracy.evidence: Checked against Common Core ELA RF.K.2c (blend and segment onsets and rimes of single-syllable spoken words), RF.K.2d (isolate and pronounce the initial, medial vowel and final sounds in CVC words) and RF.K.2e (add or substitute individual sounds to make new words), the England national curriculum Year 1 word reading statements and the DfE validated SSP criteria. Definitions follow Goswami and Bryant: the onset is the consonant or consonants before the vowel and the rime is the vowel and what follows, so sh in ship is a digraph onset and fr in frog is a two-phoneme blend onset. Every lab word was rechecked letter by letter: CVC items use one grapheme per phoneme (cat, dog, sun, pen, pin).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips: putting the vowel in the onset (do + g and shi + p get the vowel message; challenge tag toovow), splitting a digraph (s + hip prediction and challenge tag split), splitting a blend so the second consonant goes in the rime (rog, tag blend), reversing order when blending (tac prediction, tag back), naming the last heard sound as the middle (cat middle prediction t, tags firstpos and midpos), and changing the wrong position in substitution (swap feedback names which sound should change).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagrime models onset and rime structure itself: a sliding onset tile joining a rime, a fixed -ug rime with swappable onsets matched to pictures, scissors cuts between letters that must land at the vowel, first, middle and last sound positions, and a phoneme substitution grid. flagabc is letter knowledge, flagsight is sight words, flagsyl claps syllables and flagjoin is handwriting joins. The shingle gate passed against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child blends by doing it (the tile slides on and the word appears before the picture check), discovers that only the onset changes in a word family, finds by trial that every correct cut lands just before the pink vowel tile, hears each position labelled under the tiles, and makes new words by changing one tile. The done messages name the rule (the rime starts at the vowel) only after the child has done it three times.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong answers that the lab disproves: tac for c + at (the tile joins in front and reads cat), s + hip for ship (the cut after s is refused because sh is one sound), and t as the middle sound of cat (the middle tile is a). A.reveal quotes the guess in the done message.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating challenge questions with ten tagged wrong answers, each with its own correction: back (the onset comes first), vowel (the rime keeps its vowel), split (c and h make one sound), toovow (the vowel starts the rime), blend (fr is the onset), tail (the rime is the vowel and everything after), firstpos, midpos, wrongend and wrongmid (which sound to change). Lab mistakes also name the made word, for example r + ug says rug. We need bug.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short spoken sentences and real examples (Push them together and say it fast: c, at, cat!) and pass the family kid limit in validate_lessons; the adult text stays under the family limit while using the exact terms phoneme, grapheme, onset, rime, digraph, blend, CVC, initial, medial and final sound, blending, segmenting, phoneme substitution and word family.

no_filler.evidence: The filler gate passed and explanation overlap with every lesson, including Syllables, Knowing all letters and Reading High-Frequency Words by Sight, is under 12 percent. Each kid paragraph teaches one move with examples; the adult paragraphs give the standards, a glossary of terms with digraph versus blend, four named mistakes with a caution about the middle sound, and the lab outline.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots on a 360 px Android in dark and iPhone 13 in light: letter tiles are about 70 to 80 px square with large letters, pink vowel tiles keep their dot in both themes, the scissors cut lines sit between tiles with matching d | og buttons, the first, middle and last labels sit under each tile, and the swap tray of four tiles plus its four buttons fit without clipping.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark on desktop and iPhone 13, no console or page errors, all 5 Show me tasks completed and the challenge showed. Every drag or tap has a button twin (Push c onto at, picture buttons, b + ug, d | og, First: c, letter then first, middle or last), vowels differ by a dot as well as colour, and the canvas aria-label speaks each change, for example c, at: cat! Which picture is a cat?
